quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another vehicle). Use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see. Wear reflective materials to be more visible. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Not be used.
Be used on its high beam setting.
Be used on its low beam setting.
Alternate between high beam and low beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on its high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Using your high beam headlight during the day helps other drivers see you. Use your high beam any time you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding toward the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding away from the passing driver may tempt them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Exit the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars seem closer than they actually are.
Provide a narrow view of the road.
Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to convex mirrors.

questions.question: If your front wheel begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake engaged and release the rear brake.
Immediately release and re-engage the front brake.
Release the front brake and increase the pressure on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately release and re-engage the front brake.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and completely. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will do so.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, riding curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads on the back of the seat or against a sissy bar. This raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, how should it be parked?

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so approaching drivers can more easily see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Block your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely, be scratch-free, resist damage, allow clear side vision, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep pressing the front brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and slow down without braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it takes great care. When leaning into a turn, some of your tires' grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip for stopping.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: In crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the car driver not giving the rider the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
More than 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: More than 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver fails to give the rider the right-of-way.

questions.question: Who should control the speed when riding in a group?

options.text: The leader
The riders right behind the leader
The last rider
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, travel in a:

options.text: Staggered formation.
Pyramid formation.
Single-file line.
Row of pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles can ride in a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding in a lane of traffic, a motorcycle rider:

options.text: Should always ride in the same part of the lane.
Should change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Should always ride in the center of the lane.
Should always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position in the lane based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, you will have the most room to recover if you are riding in:

options.text: The left part of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right part of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most space to react if a wind blast from a passing vehicle affects your control.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week. This is part of basic motorcycle maintenance to stay safe.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, the rider should:

options.text: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning their body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: For normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. For slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans. This helps you balance.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs tell you about traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough grip. When it rains, avoid it because it becomes slippery. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and stay in the center lane.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will get scratched and brittle over time and need regular replacement.
Should be made to break away during a crash.
Should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will get scratched and brittle over time and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time, they develop scratches and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay safe and comfortable.
